title: ～たとたん — “the moment ～”
summary: Verb ta-form + とたん(に) means “the very moment A happened, B happened.” B is an unexpected or sudden event that the speaker did not control. It is used for past events.

patterns.form: 動詞た形 ＋ とたん(に)、〜
patterns.gloss: ta-form + とたん(に) (開けたとたん, 座ったとたん)

body.p: The first action is finished and, right at that instant, something else happens. Attach とたん to the ta-form of a verb: ドアを開けたとたん. The result is usually surprising or sudden.

The second part must be something that happened on its own, not a deliberate action by the speaker. A sentence like 家に着いたとたん、手を洗った (a planned action) is unnatural. Do not use it with commands or wishes either. It is also used only for past events.
～たとたん focuses on the unexpected surprise of the second event. ～たらすぐ simply means “right after,” and the second action may be intentional.

examples.ja: ドアを開（あ）けたとたん、猫（ねこ）が飛（と）び出（だ）した。
examples.romaji: Doa o aketa totan, neko ga tobidashita.
examples.tr: The moment I opened the door, the cat jumped out.

examples.ja: 席（せき）に座（すわ）ったとたん、名前（なまえ）を呼（よ）ばれた。
examples.romaji: Seki ni suwatta totan, namae o yobareta.
examples.tr: The moment I sat down, my name was called.

examples.ja: 家（いえ）を出（で）たとたん、急（きゅう）に雨（あめ）が降（ふ）り出（だ）した。
examples.romaji: Ie o deta totan, kyū ni ame ga furidashita.
examples.tr: The moment I left the house, it suddenly started to rain.

pitfalls: The second part cannot be the speaker's own deliberate action, a command or a request.
It attaches to the ta-form only, not the dictionary form. 開けるとたん is wrong.
